messages:
Ana (CSM): Hey all — prepping the onboarding SLO report for the Atlas Health renewal. Two quick asks: how do we compute latency credits during a customer’s trial -> paid cutover, and do we have a slide/template to show customers the uptime/latency credit rules?

Ben (Onboarding): For proration we use days-in-service within the billing window. So if trial ended mid-month we prorate by active days. For latency we use the monthly p95 window per the SLO definition.

Carla (Support): Agree with Ben. One caveat: if the customer was in a private deployment with custom routing we flag that for manual review — credits might need engineering sign-off.

Dinesh (Technical CSM): To be explicit: uptime credit = max(0, (SLO_target - observed_uptime) / SLO_target * monthly_fee) formula. Latency credits follow the SLA doc which buckets p95 breaches into tiers (minor/major/critical). Example tiers: 200-300ms (minor), 300-600ms (major), >600ms (critical).

Mike (Acct Exec): Helpful — customer asked for a short slide they can send to their budget team explaining how credits are calculated. Any ready-to-share one-pager?

Ben (Onboarding): I have a one-pager but it’s internal. I'll publish a cleaned version to the shared drive. Link (draft): https://redwood.docs/internal/onboard/credit-proration-draft

Ana (CSM): Can we instead point to a public-facing page or provide a sanitized PDF? Customers are sensitive about internal process links.

Dinesh (Technical CSM): We have a public PR FAQ about crediting but it doesn't show the math. Suggest we produce a 1-slide breakdown: definitions (uptime window, p95 baseline), proration rule, example calc, escalation path. I can draft the calc example:

```
Monthly fee: $10,000
SLO uptime: 99.9% target
Observed uptime: 99.5% => shortfall = 0.4% => credit = 0.004 * $10,000 = $40
```

Ben (Onboarding): Nice. For latency tier example: if p95 target is 150ms and observed p95 is 420ms, that's a major tier -> credit = 10% of monthly fee (per contract). We'll need to map those percentages from legal-approved matrix.

Carla (Support): Who owns the customer communication? If we publish a slide, need CS + Legal signoff. I can coordinate with Legal.

Ana (CSM): I'll own outreach. Plan: Dinesh drafts the slide and calc examples, Ben prepares public-friendly text, Carla pulls Legal, Mike will approve from the account perspective. Timeline: can we get a draft by EOD Thursday?

Dinesh (Technical CSM): I can have a draft by Thursday EOD. Will include: proration rule, uptime math example, latency tiers with example percents, and a short FAQ: 'what do we measure', 'how do we count downtime', 'who to contact'.

SLOBot: Summary generated — action items: Dinesh: draft slide + examples; Ben: public copy; Carla: legal request; Ana: outreach plan; Mike: account approval.

Mike (Acct Exec): Thanks — one more ask from Atlas Health: can we include a simple flow for credits during migration from hosted -> dedicated? They worry about double-counting.

Dinesh (Technical CSM): Good point. We'll add a note: migration window is excluded if it's a scheduled migration announced 5+ business days in advance; unscheduled incidents during migration are reviewed case-by-case.

Ana (CSM): Great — I'll track the PR and loop Legal. Will post the draft slide here when available. :thumbsup:
